subject: Commit phasing, banded discount and partner uplift guidance
messages:
From: Nora Patel <deals@nimbustech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthlytics.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Commit phasing and uplift request

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the numbers and want to propose a phased commit structure for our private offer to smooth cashflow across FY28. A few asks from our side:

- Can Redwood support a 4-quarter commit phasing (25% / 25% / 25% / 25%) while keeping a single private-offer SKU?
- We need clarity on partner uplift treatment — our distribution partner expects a minimum margin guarantee for the first two quarters (they asked for a 9% floor).
- How will list-price carryover and metered-burst credits interact with a phased commit?

I attached a simple model to show our expected consumption curve. Can you confirm whether the uplift guarantee is workable and what procurement evidence you need (PO schedule, reseller agreement, etc.)?

Attachments: nimbus-commit-phasing-model.xlsx (xlsx)

Appreciate a short call if easier.

Best,
Nora
Head of Partnerships
NimbusTech

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <deals@nimbustech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit phasing and uplift request

Nora — thanks for the model, that helped. High-level response and next steps below.

Summary answers:
- Yes, we can support a 4-quarter phasing on a single private-offer SKU. We’ll treat the committed quantity as an annualized allocation, and allow quarterly drawdown with reconciliation at year-end.
- Partner uplift: we can offer a guaranteed uplift floor for the distributor for the first two quarters, but it will be structured as a refundable credit if consumption exceeds the committed corridor (to avoid double-crediting). We generally cap guaranteed uplift to a fixed percentage of list price to preserve predictability — in this case we can entertain a 9% floor only if the overall discount corridor and committed ARR meet the minimum revenue threshold.
- Metered-burst and carryover: burst usage above the quarter allocation will be billed at overage rates; we can allow limited credits to be drawn from later quarters if pre-agreed in the PO schedule, but carryover beyond the annual reconciliation is uncommon.

What we need from you:
1) Confirm desired annual committed tokens/units and the quarter-by-quarter planned drawdown (I reviewed your spreadsheet but please confirm final numbers).
2) Provide a copy of the distributor margin schedule or reseller agreement showing the 9% request. If unavailable, a signed PO schedule with the proposed uplift language will suffice.
3) Confirm preferred invoice routing (Nimbus direct invoiced vs distributor invoiced and pass-through).

Proposed terms (draft, for discussion):
- 12-month private offer; annual commit with quarterly drawdown (25/25/25/25).
- Banded discount schedule: 0–50% of commit = 18% off list; 50–100% = 25% off list.
- Partner uplift floor: 9% guaranteed for Q1–Q2 only, paid as refundable credit against future invoices if usage exceeds committed corridor.
- Reconciliation: year-end true-up with final invoice adjustment.

I attached our pass-through matrix and a short example calculation. If that structure looks viable, let’s schedule a 30-minute call Monday morning to lock language for the PO and DocuSign.

Attachments: redwood-pass-through-matrix.pdf (pdf)

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Director, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: NimbusTech phasing economics (notes)

Internal notes — do not share.

Quick math: if they stick to your banded discount, the blended ASP still keeps us within the minimum ARPU target for ND-4832, but the 9% uplift floor is the risk here. If quarter 1 comes in light and we owe a refundable credit while also giving burst credits, worst-case hit could be ~6–8% of projected ARR in first half.

Options to mitigate:
- Convert Q1 guaranteed uplift into a milestone-based payout (payable only if distributor provides signed evidence of go-to-market activities).
- Add a small overage premium for metered burst in Q1 (e.g., +5% on overage) to reduce double-crediting exposure.
- Require PO schedule and reseller signature before uplift floor becomes active.

I recommend we keep the 2-quarter uplift window but condition activation on receipt of PO schedule and reseller sign-off. Ben — can you run legal on a short clause that ties the uplift guarantee to procurement evidence?

Laura
Head of Partnerships Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <deals@nimbustech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit phasing and uplift request

Nora — looping back with adjusted language after internal review. I’ve incorporated Laura’s mitigations and added a short legal trigger so we don’t create unintended exposure. Key updated points: 

1) Activation trigger: the 9% partner uplift floor for Q1–Q2 becomes effective only after Redwood receives (a) signed PO schedule specifying the quarter-by-quarter quantities and (b) the distributor’s signed reseller agreement excerpt confirming margin commitment. If both are not received prior to start of Q1, uplift protection will not apply retroactively.

2) Metered-burst handling: overage billed at standard overage rate; limited carry-forward credits allowed but capped at 10% of annual commit and only redeemable in Q3/Q4 with mutual agreement.

3) Example: with the banded discounts proposed, a Q1 under-delivery that triggers uplift credit would be offset by a holdback applied to future invoices; if they outperform annual commit, refundable uplift credits are netted in the year-end reconciliation.

Next steps: if you agree, please do the following and we’ll prepare the private-offer draft for signature:
- Send signed PO schedule (itemized by quarter)
- Upload reseller margin schedule or signed excerpt
- Confirm invoice routing: send invoices to NimbusTech finance (invoices@nimbustech.com) or to distributor (procurement@healthlytics.com).

If you'd like I can open the DocuSign envelope with the draft PO language once we have those items. Call suggestion: Monday 09:30 PT if that works.

Regards,
Karthik
Senior Director, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Nora Patel <deals@nimbustech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthlytics.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit phasing and uplift request

Karthik — this all looks sensible and we can work with the activation trigger. Quick clarifications: 

- Distributor will provide the signed reseller excerpt by Friday; procurement confirmed they can route invoices to procurement@healthlytics.com and will copy invoices@nimbustech.com.
- We accept the 10% carry-forward cap and the limited redemption window.
- One ask from our finance team: please confirm tax handling for the uplift credit (is it recorded as a credit note or a rebate for VAT/US state sales tax purposes?). We need the tax treatment on the DocuSign language.

We’ll aim to get the PO schedule over tomorrow morning and confirm the call for Monday 09:30 PT.

Thanks —
Nora
Head of Partnerships
NimbusTech
